newsitem.title: USA: PDVSA near purchase of 2 Basis refineries in Texas.
newsitem.headline: PDVSA near purchase of 2 Basis refineries in Texas.

text.p: State Petroleos de Venezuela is closing in on a deal to buy two refineries in Texas owned by Basis Petroleum, the refining arm of Wall Street brokerage house Salomon Inc, a PDVSA source said Wednesday.
The negotiations are "very advanced" and should be completed "very soon," the source said.
Top officials from Corpoven, the PDVSA subsidiary through which the deal is being conducted, are now wrapping up final negotiations in the U.S., the source added.
PDVSA is negotiating to buy two of three Basis plants on the Gulf Coast: a 125,000 barrel per day (bpd) refinery in Texas City and a 68,000 bpd facility in Houston.
The source did not disclose the value of the refineries, but said PDVSA would sign "one deal for the two (plants)."
The plants' value depends on how they are analyzed, he said. The refineries' worth would differ, for example, whether they are viewed as ongoing businesses or fixed assets.
Although Corpoven is conducting the negotiations, the refineries are likely to come under the ownership of one of PDVSA's U.S. subsidiaries, either PDV America or Citgo Petroleum, the source said.
Most of the Venezuelan crude that the refineries would process, however, would likely be Corpoven's, he added.
PDVSA has three integrated operating subsidiaries: Corpoven, Maraven and Lagoven.
The impending purchase is part of PDVSA's long-term efforts to secure more downstream outlets for its growing crude production, which now stands at more than three million bpd.
Under its 10-year plan, PDVSA plans to expand refining capacity from 2.9 million bpd in 1997 to 3.5 million bpd in 2006, of which 2.1 million bpd would be based outside Venezuela.
Currently, PDVSA has 1.55 million bpd of refining capacity outside Venezuela, including facilities in the U.S., Europe and the Caribbean. --Patricia Garip-Bertuol NY Energy Desk ((+1 212 859 1620))
